definitions.explanation: Describes two things so deeply connected that they cannot be considered separately.

examples.japanese: この{二|ふた}つは{切|き}り{離|はな}せない{関係|かんけい}だ。
examples.english: These two have an inseparable relationship.

examples.japanese: {経済|けいざい}と{環境|かんきょう}は{切|き}り{離|はな}せない。
examples.english: The economy and the environment are inseparable.

examples.japanese: {日本|にほん}の{文化|ぶんか}と{四季|しき}は{切|き}り{離|はな}せない{関係|かんけい}にある。
examples.english: Japanese culture and the four seasons are inextricably linked.

notes:
The negative potential form of {切|き}り{離|はな}す (to separate; to detach), used as a set expression meaning "cannot be separated" or "inseparable." Commonly used to describe deep connections between concepts, people, or things.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- AとBは{切|き}り{離|はな}せない: A and B are inseparable
- {切|き}り{離|はな}せない{関係|かんけい}: an inseparable relationship
- ～から{切|き}り{離|はな}せない: inseparable from ~

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {不可分|ふかぶん}: indivisible — more formal and academic
- {密接|みっせつ}な{関係|かんけい}: a close relationship — similar but less emphatic
- {表裏一体|ひょうりいったい}: two sides of the same coin
